claim_verdicts.evidence: Docs: 'the Deployment controller changes the actual state to the desired state at a controlled rate. You can define Deployments to create new ReplicaSets' and note 'Do not manage ReplicaSets owned by a Deployment.' Execution (deployment.txt, server v1.34.11): one apply of web-deployment.yaml lists deployment.apps/web, replicaset.apps/web-... and three pod/web-...-...; server dry-run of the manifest on v1.34.11: 'deployment.apps/web created (server dry run)'.

Docs: 'Notice that the name of the ReplicaSet is always formatted as [DEPLOYMENT-NAME]-[HASH]. This name will become the basis for the Pods which are created. The HASH string is the same as the pod-template-hash label on the ReplicaSet.' and 'It is generated by hashing the PodTemplate of the ReplicaSet'. Live cluster (v1.34.11): ReplicaSet redis-59c7789868 has pod-template-hash=59c7789868; its Pod has generateName 'redis-59c7789868-' and name redis-59c7789868-zp5qw.
claim_verdicts.source: refs/kubernetes-website .../controllers/deployment.md (Creating a Deployment; Pod-template-hash label); kubectl get rs,pod -n donhang -l app=redis

claim_verdicts.evidence: Docs note: 'A Deployment's rollout is triggered if and only if the Deployment's Pod template (that is, .spec.template) is changed ... Other updates, such as scaling the Deployment, do not trigger a rollout.' Execution (deployment.txt): after apply with replicas: 5, 'kubectl get replicaset -l app=web' shows a single 'web-... 5 5 5' and 'Pods from before the change still running: 3 of 3'.

Docs: 'By default, Kubernetes uses background cascading deletion unless you manually use foreground deletion or choose to orphan the dependent objects.' and 'By default, Kubernetes deletes dependent objects.' Execution (deployment.txt): after 'kubectl delete deployment web -n donhang', 'kubectl get replicaset,pods -n donhang -l app=web' -> 'No resources found in donhang namespace.' Pod replacement: same ReplicaSet controller behaviour shown in replicaset.txt.

Docs: 'some objects are owners of other objects. For example, a ReplicaSet is the owner of a set of Pods.' 'Kubernetes sets the value of this field automatically for objects that are dependents of other objects like ReplicaSets, ... Deployments'; Deployment docs: ReplicaSets a Deployment 'creates or adopts' (so 'usually the one that created it' is right). Live v1.34.11: redis-59c7789868 <- Deployment/redis; redis-59c7789868-zp5qw <- ReplicaSet/redis-59c7789868.
claim_verdicts.source: refs/kubernetes-website .../working-with-objects/owners-dependents.md; .../controllers/deployment.md l.24,159; kubectl get rs,pods -n donhang -o jsonpath ownerReferences

claim_verdicts.evidence: Docs: 'type: Available with status: "True" means that your Deployment has minimum availability. Minimum availability is dictated by the parameters specified in the deployment strategy.' Execution (deployment.txt): 'kubectl wait --for=condition=Available deployment/web ...' -> 'deployment.apps/web condition met', followed by READY 3/3.

Docs: 'READY displays how many replicas of the application are available to your users. It follows the pattern ready/desired.' 'UP-TO-DATE displays the number of replicas that have been updated to achieve the desired state.' Output header in deployment.txt: 'NAME READY UP-TO-DATE AVAILABLE AGE'.

Docs: 'Do not overlap labels or selectors with other controllers (including other Deployments and StatefulSets). Kubernetes doesn't stop you from overlapping, and if multiple controllers have overlapping selectors those controllers might conflict and behave unexpectedly.' Lesson wording 'could conflict with it over the same Pods' stays within this.

issues.text: Same over-generalisation fixed in section 2 now reappears in misconception 2: the top level of deploy/k8s/ at stage-2 also holds api-configmap.yaml (ConfigMap), namespace.yaml (Namespace) and kind-config.yaml (kind Cluster), so not all manifests there 'turn out to be Deployments'. 'with no ReplicaSet among them' is true.
issues.quote: You notice this when Đơn Hàng's own manifests at the top of `deploy/k8s/` turn out to be Deployments, with no ReplicaSet among them.
issues.fix: Change to: "You notice this when Đơn Hàng's own workloads in `deploy/k8s/`, such as `api.yaml` and `db.yaml`, are Deployments, with no ReplicaSet manifest among them."
